Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml dropped to root of recovery partition (GreatXML staging)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Defender Offline Scan scheduled then immediate WinRE reboot (GreatXML pre-condition + trigger) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BitLocker FVE policy or service registry tamper (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] BitLocker protector enumeration or suspension via manage-bde / WMI (post-bypass) · [LLM] BitLocker recovery key export via manage-bde -protectors -get or AD msFVE-RecoveryInformation query · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml dropped to root of recovery partition (GreatXML staging) AIWeaponization High
Hunts the GreatXML staging step: an unattend.xml file or a Recovery/WindowsRE/ReAgent.xml file written to the root of the Windows recovery partition. This is the article's exact pre-condition for the BitLocker bypass and is not a normal Windows servicing path for user-context processes. Rationale: Article body explicitly names both filenames and target location: "Copy an XML file ('unattend.xml') and a recovery folder containing another XML file ('Recovery/WindowsRE/ReAgent.xml) to the root of the recovery partition." Filename + path combo is the highest-fidelity pivot in the article. Cross-checked Microsoft's ReAgent.xml documentation (servicing-stack only writes it during cumulative updates via TiWorker/ReAgentc). Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/windows-recovery-environment--windows-re--technical-reference
ATT&CKT1542.001 T1564.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cumulative Windows Update servicing operations (TiWorker/ReAgentc) - excluded
  • Manual IT rebuild of WinRE via reagentc /setreimage
  • Imaging tools (DISM, MDT) refreshing the recovery image
  • Backup software snapshotting WindowsRE.wim contents
  • OEM recovery refresh utilities (Dell SupportAssist, HP Recovery Manager)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TiWorker.exe","ReAgentc.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","DismHost.exe","setup.exe","wuauclt.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the DeviceName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, and process tree back to the grandparent. Confirm whether the writing process is a user-launched shell/script vs a signed Microsoft servicing binary; check whether the device is in an active patch window or imaging task. Step 2 (contain): If the process lineage is user-context (cmd, powershell, explorer launching a copy), isolate the device in Defender for Endpoint and force a logout. Block subsequent boot to WinRE via group policy or BitLocker re-encryption command. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep the org for any other host where unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml landed on Recovery/EFI paths in the last 30d, look for prior DeviceEvents indicating Defender Offline Scan was scheduled (article's pre-condition), and check WinRE boot indicators (BCD edits, bootmgr reboot codes).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Recovery\", @"\WindowsRE\", @"\EFI\", "HarddiskVolume")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TiWorker.exe","ReAgentc.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated" or EventType == "FileModified"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Recovery\", @"\WindowsRE\", @"\EFI\", "HarddiskVolume")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TiWorker.exe","ReAgentc.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath
title: GreatXML BitLocker bypass staging - unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml in recovery partition
id: 7e3b5f2c-9d4a-4f1b-8d6c-2e0a3b9f1c4e
description: Detects file creation of unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml at the root of the Windows recovery partition, the exact staging step for the GreatXML BitLocker bypass disclosed by Chaotic Eclipse.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1542.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\unattend.xml'
      - '\ReAgent.xml'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Recovery\'
      - '\WindowsRE\'
      - 'HarddiskVolume'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\ReAgentc.exe'
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\Recovery\\*\\unattend.xml OR *\\WindowsRE\\ReAgent.xml OR *\\recovery\\*\\unattend.xml OR *\\windowsre\\reagent.xml)) -@Image:(*\\TiWorker.exe OR *\\ReAgentc.exe OR *\\TrustedInstaller.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\(Recovery|WindowsRE|EFI)\\.*\\(unattend|ReAgent)\.xml$/i
| ContextImageFileName!=/\\(TiWorker|ReAgentc|TrustedInstaller)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.process_name) as process from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" OR Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\WindowsRE\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="\\Device\\HarddiskVolume*\\unattend.xml") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where process!="TiWorker.exe" AND process!="ReAgentc.exe"
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.process_name) as process from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" OR Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\WindowsRE\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="\\Device\\HarddiskVolume*\\unattend.xml") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where process!="TiWorker.exe" AND process!="ReAgentc.exe"
Defender Offline Scan scheduled then immediate WinRE reboot (GreatXML pre-condition + trigger) AIExploitation Medium
GreatXML requires the host to have used Windows Defender Offline Scan to pre-stage WinRE, then a Shift+Restart boot into WinRE. This hunts the temporal correlation: WdBoot/MpCmdRun scheduling an offline scan followed by a reboot-to-recovery within minutes. Rationale: Article: "If Defender offline scan was never initiated then you have to either login and initiate it yourself or figure out a way to boot into WinRE in offline scan state" and "Reboot to Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) by holding Shift while clicking Restart". The temporal pair of WDOScan-arm followed by /boottore or shutdown /o is the article-specific trigger sequence. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/microsoft-defender-offline
ATT&CKT1542.001 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate user running Defender Offline Scan from Windows Security UI then restarting
  • IT helpdesk troubleshooting suspected rootkit with offline scan + reboot
  • Patch-Tuesday automation that schedules WDOScan followed by reboot
  • Endpoint hardening playbook test runs
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the AccountName is a real user (not SYSTEM/$). Pull DeviceInfo to check whether the device has BitLocker enabled and whether it joined the recovery partition pre-condition (file-event UC fires alongside). Step 2 (contain): If the WinRE boot occurred, mark the device as potentially-compromised - assume disk content was read in clear text. Re-encrypt with a new BitLocker key, rotate any credentials cached on disk (RDP creds, browser secrets, DPAPI master keys). Step 3 (hunt): Search DeviceFileEvents on the same DeviceId in the prior 24h for the unattend.xml/ReAgent.xml staging (paired UC). Sweep the fleet for other devices where a WDOScan was scheduled but never followed by a real scan completion event.
let WindowMinutes = 15m;
let OfflineScanScheduled = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where (FileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-WDEnable","WDOScan","OfflineScan"))
         or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
    | project ScanTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ScanCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ScanUser = AccountName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (FileName =~ "shutdown.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/o")
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Restart-Computer -WinRE","reagentc /boottore"))
     or (FileName =~ "reagentc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/boottore")
| join kind=inner OfflineScanScheduled on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (ScanTime .. ScanTime + WindowMinutes)
| project ScanTime, RebootTime = Timestamp, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ScanTime), DeviceName, AccountName, ScanCmd, ProcessCommandLine
| order by RebootTime desc
let WindowMinutes = 15m;
let OfflineScanScheduled = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\MpCmdRun.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("-WDEnable","WDOScan","OfflineScan")
       or  (NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
    | project ScanTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, ScanCmd = CommandLine, ScanUser = SubjectUserName;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith "\\shutdown.exe" and CommandLine has "/o")
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\reagentc.exe" and CommandLine has "/boottore")
     or CommandLine has "Restart-Computer -WinRE"
| join kind=inner OfflineScanScheduled on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (ScanTime .. ScanTime + WindowMinutes)
| project ScanTime, RebootTime = TimeGenerated, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, ScanTime), Computer, SubjectUserName, ScanCmd, CommandLine
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 (@Image:(*\\shutdown.exe OR *\\Shutdown.exe) AND @CommandLine:*\/o*) OR (@Image:(*\\reagentc.exe OR *\\ReAgentc.exe) AND @CommandLine:*\/boottore*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\shutdown\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\s\/o(\s|$)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\reagentc\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\/boottore/i) OR CommandLine=/Restart-Computer\s+-WinRE/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="MpCmdRun.exe" Processes.process="*-WDEnable*") OR (Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" Processes.process="*/o*") OR (Processes.process_name="PowerShell.exe" Processes.process="*Start-MpWDOScan*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | transaction dest maxspan=10m | where eventcount>=2
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="MpCmdRun.exe" Processes.process="*-WDEnable*") OR (Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" Processes.process="*/o*") OR (Processes.process_name="PowerShell.exe" Processes.process="*Start-MpWDOScan*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | transaction dest maxspan=10m | where eventcount>=2
BitLocker protector enumeration or suspension via manage-bde / WMI (post-bypass) AIActions on Objectives High
After regaining shell with BitLocker volume mounted, the attacker typically suspends BitLocker, dumps recovery keys, or enumerates protectors. Hunts manage-bde flags and the Win32_EncryptableVolume WMI surface that adversaries use to weaken the encryption after the GreatXML bypass. Rationale: GreatXML grants shell with the BitLocker volume mounted; the natural follow-on is to suspend BitLocker (-off/-pause), dump protectors (-protectors -get), or trigger recovery mode (-forcerecovery). manage-bde flags and the WMI Win32_EncryptableVolume surface are documented Microsoft APIs - matches are extremely high-signal when the parent isn't an MDM agent. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/operations-guide • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/001/
ATT&CKT1542.001 T1555.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Helpdesk technician suspending BitLocker for firmware/TPM update
  • Intune/SCCM/ccmexec.exe rotating recovery keys (filtered)
  • BitLocker status reporting scripts run by compliance tools
  • User initiating BitLocker recovery via Settings UI
  • Imaging task suspending BitLocker before disk capture
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe","MDMAgent.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Determine whether the executing user has device-admin entitlement and whether an Intune/SCCM job is scheduled in this window. Pull manage-bde -status output via a live response session to see protector state. Step 2 (contain): If un-sanctioned, isolate the device, force a BitLocker re-enable with a new key, and rotate any AD/Entra recovery key escrow. Step 3 (hunt): Correlate with the WinRE-boot UC and the recovery-partition file-drop UC on the same DeviceId. Look for downstream credential access (lsass dump, ntds.dit copy, DPAPI master-key access) since the disk was readable in cleartext.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "manage-bde.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any (" -off"," -pause"," -protectors -get"," -protectors -disable"," -forcerecovery"," -recoverykey"))
   or  (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Disable-BitLocker","Suspend-BitLocker","Win32_EncryptableVolume","GetKeyProtectors","DecryptVolume","BackupToRecoveryServices"))
   or  (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "encryptablevolume")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MDMAgent.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe","ccmexec.exe","MpCmdRun.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessTokenElevation, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith "\\manage-bde.exe" and CommandLine has_any (" -off"," -pause"," -protectors -get"," -protectors -disable"," -forcerecovery"," -recoverykey"))
   or  (NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("Disable-BitLocker","Suspend-BitLocker","Win32_EncryptableVolume","GetKeyProtectors","DecryptVolume"))
   or  (NewProcessName endswith "\\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "encryptablevolume")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "\\ccmexec.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\IntuneManagementExtension.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
title: BitLocker protector enumeration or suspension after recovery bypass
id: 5c1e2d8b-3f47-4e6a-b9c4-7d2f1a8e3b5d
description: Detects manage-bde, PowerShell BitLocker cmdlets, or WMI Win32_EncryptableVolume calls that suspend, disable, or enumerate BitLocker protectors - common post-bypass step in the GreatXML chain.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1542.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  managebde:
    Image|endswith: '\manage-bde.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -off'
      - ' -pause'
      - ' -protectors -get'
      - ' -protectors -disable'
      - ' -forcerecovery'
  pwsh_bitlocker:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Disable-BitLocker'
      - 'Suspend-BitLocker'
      - 'Win32_EncryptableVolume'
      - 'GetKeyProtectors'
      - 'DecryptVolume'
  wmic_bitlocker:
    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'encryptablevolume'
  filter_mdm:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\ccmexec.exe'
      - '\IntuneManagementExtension.exe'
      - '\MDMAgent.exe'
  condition: (managebde or pwsh_bitlocker or wmic_bitlocker) and not filter_mdm
level: high
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 ((@Image:(*\\manage-bde.exe OR *\\Manage-bde.exe OR *\\MANAGE-BDE.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*\-off* OR *\-pause* OR *"-protectors -get"* OR *"-protectors -disable"* OR *\-forcerecovery*)) OR (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*Disable-BitLocker* OR *Suspend-BitLocker* OR *Win32_EncryptableVolume* OR *GetKeyProtectors* OR *DecryptVolume*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\manage-bde\.exe$/i CommandLine=/(\s-off\b|\s-pause\b|-protectors\s+-get|-protectors\s+-disable|-forcerecovery|-recoverykey)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/(Disable-BitLocker|Suspend-BitLocker|Win32_EncryptableVolume|GetKeyProtectors|DecryptVolume)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\wmic\.exe$/i CommandLine=/encryptablevolume/i)
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/(ccmexec|IntuneManagementExtension|MDMAgent)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="manage-bde.exe" (Processes.process="*-off*" OR Processes.process="*-pause*" OR Processes.process="*-protectors -get*" OR Processes.process="*-protectors -disable*" OR Processes.process="*-forcerecovery*")) OR (Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" (Processes.process="*Disable-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Suspend-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Win32_EncryptableVolume*" OR Processes.process="*GetKeyProtectors*" OR Processes.process="*DecryptVolume*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="manage-bde.exe" (Processes.process="*-off*" OR Processes.process="*-pause*" OR Processes.process="*-protectors -get*" OR Processes.process="*-protectors -disable*" OR Processes.process="*-forcerecovery*")) OR (Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" (Processes.process="*Disable-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Suspend-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Win32_EncryptableVolume*" OR Processes.process="*GetKeyProtectors*" OR Processes.process="*DecryptVolume*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
BitLocker FVE policy or service registry tamper (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE) AIInstallation High
Disabling BitLocker enforcement via Group Policy registry keys or the FVE service registry path lets an attacker keep the volume decrypted across reboots after the GreatXML bypass. Hunts writes to the BitLocker policy and service registry hives by non-policy processes. Rationale: FVE is the documented BitLocker registry surface (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE and HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\FVE). After the GreatXML bypass grants attacker write access to the live volume, the cleanest persistence is to push policy keys that disable re-encryption enforcement. Excluded gpupdate / TrustedInstaller / Intune which are the only legitimate writers. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/configure
ATT&CKT1112 T1542.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Group Policy refresh applying a new BitLocker baseline
  • Intune compliance policy adjusting BitLocker settings
  • SCCM hardening baseline run
  • Manual admin tweaking BitLocker policy via gpedit.msc
  • Microsoft Security Baseline import via LGPO tool
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("gpupdate.exe","GPOSvc.exe","svchost.exe","TiWorker.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe","ccmexec.exe","LGPO.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Snapshot the current FVE policy state (gpresult /h, reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE) and compare to the gold image. Identify the InitiatingProcessFileName and account. Step 2 (contain): Force re-application of the BitLocker policy GPO, re-enable BitLocker on all volumes (manage-bde -on), and rotate recovery keys to AD/Entra. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the DeviceId across the other GreatXML UCs (recovery-partition file drop, WinRE-boot pair, manage-bde suspension). Sweep the org for other devices where FVE policy was changed by the same process or account.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated","RegistryValueDeleted")
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Policies\Microsoft\FVE", @"\Services\FVE", @"\Policies\Microsoft\TPM")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("gpupdate.exe","GPOSvc.exe","svchost.exe","TiWorker.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe","ccmexec.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","explorer.exe","reagentc.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Policies\Microsoft\FVE", @"\Services\FVE", @"\Policies\Microsoft\TPM")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("gpupdate.exe","svchost.exe","TiWorker.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe","ccmexec.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
title: BitLocker FVE policy/service registry tamper
id: a7b3c9e1-4d62-4f5a-9c8e-2b1d5f7a3e8c
description: Detects modification of HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE or the FVE service hive by non-policy processes, a common follow-on after the GreatXML BitLocker bypass.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1112
  - attack.t1542.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\'
      - '\Services\FVE\'
      - '\Policies\Microsoft\TPM\'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\gpupdate.exe'
      - '\svchost.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\IntuneManagementExtension.exe'
      - '\ccmexec.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\Policies\\Microsoft\\FVE\\* OR *\\policies\\microsoft\\fve\\* OR *\\Services\\FVE\\* OR *\\services\\fve\\*) -@Image:(*\\gpupdate.exe OR *\\svchost.exe OR *\\TiWorker.exe OR *\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\IntuneManagementExtension.exe OR *\\ccmexec.exe)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\(Policies\\Microsoft\\FVE|Services\\FVE|Policies\\Microsoft\\TPM)\\/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(gpupdate|svchost|TiWorker|TrustedInstaller|IntuneManagementExtension|ccmexec)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as data values(Registry.process_name) as process from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\FVE\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\FVE\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\WindowsUpdate\\OSUpgrade\\*") by Registry.dest Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | where process!="GPOSvc.exe" AND process!="gpupdate.exe" AND process!="svchost.exe"
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as data values(Registry.process_name) as process from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\FVE\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\FVE\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\WindowsUpdate\\OSUpgrade\\*") by Registry.dest Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | where process!="GPOSvc.exe" AND process!="gpupdate.exe" AND process!="svchost.exe"
BitLocker recovery key export via manage-bde -protectors -get or AD msFVE-RecoveryInformation query AIActions on Objectives Medium
Successful BitLocker bypass requires key material. Hunts on-host manage-bde recovery-key extraction and LDAP queries against msFVE-RecoveryInformation in AD, which is the standard escrow object an attacker would exfiltrate to keep persistent disk access. Rationale: Article frames GreatXML as a BitLocker bypass; the practical attacker follow-on is to extract or escrow-query the recovery key so the bypass survives reboot. msFVE-RecoveryInformation is the well-known AD object class storing recovery keys (Microsoft docs + ATT&CK T1555.004). manage-bde -protectors -get is the documented export command. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/recovery-overview • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/004/
ATT&CKT1555.004 T1552.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Helpdesk staff retrieving recovery key for legitimate user lockout
  • MBAM/SCCM compliance scan querying recovery key escrow
  • Audit script enumerating BitLocker state across endpoints
  • Decommissioning workflow extracting keys before disk wipe
  • Backup/imaging tooling enumerating protectors
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MBAMAgent.exe","BitLockerManagementHandler.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe","ccmexec.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify who ran the command and whether they have helpdesk/key-recovery entitlement. Pull surrounding process activity to detect chained recovery-key write-to-disk or upload (curl, certutil, smbclient). Step 2 (contain): If the actor isn't authorised, rotate the BitLocker recovery key for that device immediately (manage-bde -protectors -delete then -add) and force re-encryption with the new key. Step 3 (hunt): Look across AD/Entra for the same identity querying msFVE recovery objects for OTHER devices in the prior 90d (lateral key harvesting). Correlate with the other GreatXML UCs on the same host.
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where (FileName =~ "manage-bde.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has " -protectors -get")
     or  (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("KeyProtector","msFVE-RecoveryInformation","Get-ADObject","Get-BitLockerVolume"))
     or  (FileName in~ ("dsquery.exe","ldifde.exe","csvde.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("msFVE","FVE-Recovery"))
  | where AccountName !endswith "$"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
),
(IdentityQueryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where Query has_any ("msFVE-RecoveryInformation","msFVE-RecoveryPassword","msFVE-KeyPackage")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Query, QueryTarget, Protocol
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where (NewProcessName endswith "\\manage-bde.exe" and CommandLine has " -protectors -get")
     or  (NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("KeyProtector","msFVE-RecoveryInformation","Get-BitLockerVolume"))
  | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID in (4662,5136)
  | where ObjectName has_any ("msFVE-RecoveryInformation","msFVE-RecoveryPassword")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ObjectName, AccessMask
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp

    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] CodeIgniter4 ext_in Bypass — PHP File Written to Public Upload Directory by Web Server
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] HTTP Access to PHP File Inside CodeIgniter4 Upload Directory (Webshell Trigger)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Webshell Execution — PHP/Web Server Process Spawning Shell After ext_in Bypass
CodeIgniter4 ext_in Bypass — PHP File Written to Public Upload Directory by Web Server AIInstallation High
Hunts the outcome of CVE-2026-48062: a web server / PHP interpreter (php-fpm, php, httpd, nginx, w3wp) writing a PHP-executable file (.php/.phtml/.phar/.phps/.inc) into a publicly-served upload path (public/uploads, public/avatar, writable/uploads, /var/www/*/uploads). This is the smoking-gun artefact of the ext_in MIME-vs-extension validation flaw described in the GHSA — the malicious shell.php with GIF-like content lands on disk. Rationale: Anchored on three article-specific strings: the affected framework's directory layout (public/, writable/uploads — explicitly named in the workarounds), the file-extension allow-list (php/phtml/phar/phps/inc — the executable types ext_in was supposed to block), and the parent process set characteristic of CodeIgniter4 deployments (php-fpm / php / httpd / nginx / w3wp). The combination of web-server-process + PHP-extension + public upload path is what makes this article-specific and not a generic webshell rule.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Composer install / `composer update` writing vendor PHP into the docroot under public/ (not under uploads/) — path filter excludes it
  • Static site generators or CMS plugin installers writing PHP into framework paths (admin/, themes/, plugins/) — path filter excludes it
  • Cache warmer writing compiled PHP into writable/cache or writable/sessions (not writable/uploads)
  • Image processors (Intervention/Image, Imagine) writing thumbnail files where the configured extension list accidentally lets .php through
  • CI/CD deployer (capistrano, deployer.php) syncing PHP files to /public/ during release
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !has "/vendor/" and FolderPath !has "\\vendor\\" and FolderPath !has "/writable/cache" and FolderPath !has "/writable/sessions" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "composer"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the offending file path and `file` / `head -c 16` it — confirm GIF89a/GIF87a or other image magic bytes followed by `<?php` further in. Pull the parent web request from access logs (~5s window around Timestamp) to identify the source IP and the upload endpoint. Step 2 (contain): remove the file, revoke the active web session token used to upload it, and block the source IP at the WAF. If the host has been exploited, isolate it from the network. Step 3 (hunt): grep the same parent process for other recent file writes with non-image extensions in upload paths; query access logs for prior 4xx upload attempts from the same IP/UA (bypass-discovery activity); confirm the affected CodeIgniter4 install is < 4.7.3 and force-patch.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".phps" or FileName endswith ".inc"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/public/uploads","/public/avatar","/writable/uploads","/var/www","/htdocs/uploads",@"\public\uploads",@"\public\avatar",@"\writable\uploads",@"\wwwroot\uploads")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php","php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-cgi","httpd.exe","httpd","nginx.exe","nginx","apache2","w3wp.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","phar","phps","inc")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/public/uploads","/public/avatar","/writable/uploads","/var/www","\\public\\uploads","\\public\\avatar","\\writable\\uploads","\\wwwroot\\uploads")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php","php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","nginx","apache2","w3wp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername

Webshell Execution — PHP/Web Server Process Spawning Shell After ext_in Bypass AIActions on Objectives High
Detects post-exploitation execution of the shell.php (or equivalent) dropped via CVE-2026-48062: a PHP interpreter or web server process (php, php-fpm, httpd, nginx, w3wp) spawning a command-line shell, recon utility, or downloader. The article confirms the bypass leads to arbitrary code execution from PHP files in web-accessible directories — this is the runtime symptom. Rationale: The article explicitly states the bypass 'may lead to arbitrary code execution'. Any execution path from a web-tier process to a shell/recon binary is the runtime smoking gun. The parent process list is anchored to the deployment binaries CodeIgniter4 actually runs under (php-fpm/php-cgi for PHP-FPM stacks, httpd/nginx as reverse proxy + execve, w3wp.exe on IIS).
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.001 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PHP cron job invoking ImageMagick / ffmpeg via shell_exec for media processing
  • phpMyAdmin / Adminer / Roundcube running shell tasks (set_time_limit, backup features) on operator-controlled hosts
  • Composer hook in a deployment pipeline running `git`, `npm`, or shell helpers under php-fpm
  • WordPress plugin auto-update invoking `tar` / `unzip` via PHP exec
  • Monitoring agents (Munin, Cacti) that run `uname`/`whoami` via a PHP web UI
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("artisan","composer.phar","wp-cli.phar","drush") and FileName in~ ("sh","bash","git","npm"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the parent process's loaded script path — for php-fpm this is in /proc/<pid>/cmdline or the web-server access log timestamp-matched to the spawn; the script path will point at the dropped shell. Pull the child command line and its child processes for the next 5 minutes. Step 2 (contain): kill the child + parent worker, isolate the host, rotate any credentials accessible to the web service account (DB password in CodeIgniter4 .env / Database.php config). Step 3 (hunt): cross-reference UC1 hits to identify other dropped PHP files on the same host, scan all CodeIgniter4 installs for unexpected files in public/uploads and public/avatar, check egress for the same RemoteIPs the child process contacted.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php","php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-cgi","httpd.exe","httpd","nginx.exe","nginx","apache2","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","python","python.exe","python3","curl","curl.exe","wget","whoami","whoami.exe","id","uname","net.exe","systeminfo.exe","nc","ncat","mshta.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildPath = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php","php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","nginx","apache2","w3wp.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","python","python3","curl","wget","whoami","id","uname","nc","ncat","net.exe","systeminfo.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash

HTTP Access to PHP File Inside CodeIgniter4 Upload Directory (Webshell Trigger) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the access pattern that triggers the dropped webshell after a successful CVE-2026-48062 ext_in bypass: an HTTP GET or POST returning 2xx to a .php / .phtml / .phar file located under /uploads/, /avatar/, or /writable/uploads/. Under a secure deployment those paths should serve only image/static assets — a 200 response on a PHP file there means the framework has executed user-uploaded code. Rationale: The article identifies the executable extensions (PHP and 'other executable files') and the deployment shape (uploads under public web root) that make this access pattern uniquely dangerous. Hitting a .php under /uploads/ or /avatar/ with a 2xx is not a normal CodeIgniter4 traffic pattern — image-processing endpoints sit at controller routes like /index.php/avatar/show, not at /public/uploads/foo.php directly.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy timthumb.php / similar image-resize scripts deliberately deployed under /avatar/
  • File-manager UIs (elFinder, KCFinder) whose admin entry-point lives under /uploads/file_manager.php
  • CMS plugins that serve dynamic PHP from /uploads/ as a design choice (uncommon but exists)
  • Synthetic uptime monitors hitting a placeholder /uploads/healthcheck.php endpoint
  • Developer testing immediately post-deploy hitting /public/uploads/index.php
Suppression filter
| where url !endswith "/index.php" and url !contains "/avatar/timthumb" and url !contains "/uploads/file_manager"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the source IP, user-agent, and full URL including query string — webshells commonly take commands via ?cmd=, ?c=, ?0=, or POST bodies. Pull the matching DeviceFileEvent (UC1) to confirm when the file landed and which process wrote it. Step 2 (contain): block source IP at WAF/edge, remove the PHP file from the upload directory, rotate the web service account credentials and any secrets readable by it. Step 3 (hunt): for the source IP, hunt the prior 24h for failed (4xx) POSTs to /upload* endpoints (bypass discovery attempts); for the file, hunt all hosts in the org for sibling .php files in the same upload dir; confirm CodeIgniter4 version < 4.7.3 and patch.
let upload_php = dynamic([@"/uploads/",@"/avatar/",@"/writable/uploads/",@"/public/uploads/",@"/public/avatar/"]);
let php_ext = dynamic([".php",".phtml",".phar",".phps",".inc"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where csMethod in ("GET","POST")
     | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)
     | where csUriStem has_any (upload_php)
     | where csUriStem has_any (php_ext)
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, srcIP=cIP, http_method=csMethod, url=strcat(csUriStem,iif(isempty(csUriQuery),"",strcat("?",csUriQuery))), status=scStatus, ua=csUserAgent, referer=csReferer),
    (ImWebSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
     | where HttpMethod in~ ("GET","POST")
     | where Url has_any (upload_php)
     | where Url has_any (php_ext)
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, srcIP=SrcIpAddr, http_method=HttpMethod, url=Url, status=HttpStatusCode, ua=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, referer=HttpRequestHeaderReferer))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName

SecurityEvent

| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),

         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
