SPECTRALVIPER known-sample SHA1 execution or filesystem write AIInstallation High
Alerts whenever a process executes or a file is written whose SHA1 matches one of the 20 SPECTRALVIPER / OceanLotus stager and dropper hashes ESET published. Covers both SPECTRALVIPER backdoor binaries and the malicious FireAnt Metakit update payloads from the supply-chain wave. Rationale: All 20 SHA1s are pulled directly from the IOC block of the ESET report and correspond to SPECTRALVIPER samples (both old reused first-iteration samples and fresh stable-version samples from Table 1) plus the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain droppers. Hash match on process + filesystem + image-load catches dropper, persistent loader, and DLL side-load variants.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender / CrowdStrike sample-submission VMs ingesting the IOC bundle for testing
  • DFIR teams replaying confirmed malware samples during tabletop exercises
  • VirusTotal / hybrid-analysis collector hosts that store hash archives
  • Security researcher endpoints reverse-engineering the samples
  • Backup/restore restoring a previously-quarantined sample from shadow copy
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !has "sandbox" and DeviceName !has "malware" and DeviceName !has "detonation"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: identify whether the host is a known malware-analysis sandbox or a production endpoint — check device tags, OU membership and the user profile of InitiatingProcessAccountName. If production, this is a confirmed-malicious detection with no investigation needed before action. 2) CONTAIN: network-isolate the device, kill the process tree, quarantine the binary, force credential rotation for any account with an interactive logon to that host in the last 90 days, and block the SHA1 across the EDR fleet via Indicators of Compromise policy. 3) HUNT: for every host that ran one of these hashes, pull DeviceNetworkEvents and DnsEvents 30 days back looking for the six SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains and eight IPs; check FireAnt Metakit install history; pivot on the InitiatingProcessFolderPath to identify the dropper that wrote the sample.

union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where SHA1 in~ (ioc_sha1) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in~ (ioc_sha1)
  | project Timestamp, Table="Process", DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine),

FireAnt Metakit supply-chain: update binary spawning unusual child AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for the FireAnt Metakit application (the Vietnamese stock-investment platform whose update server OceanLotus compromised from Oct-2025 to Mar-2026) spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or unsigned binaries from temp/AppData. This is the textbook detection shape for the supply-chain payload that ESET observed delivering SPECTRALVIPER after a poisoned update. Rationale: ESET explicitly names FireAnt Metakit as the compromised stock-trading platform and describes the update-server-replaced-with-malicious-payload pattern; any FireAnt Metakit process spawning a script interpreter, LOLBin, or binary out of temp/AppData is the operational shape of the supply-chain payload chain that ends in SPECTRALVIPER drop. Hunting tier because FireAnt's own update process may legitimately invoke some installer LOLBins on first install.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt Metakit update invoking msiexec.exe during a real product update
  • FireAnt installer writing helper binaries to %TEMP% as part of normal first-run installation
  • Endpoint backup software (Veeam, Acronis) interacting with FireAnt install directory during scheduled backup
  • User troubleshooting FireAnt by running it from a portable/extracted location in Downloads
  • Antivirus / DLP scanning FireAnt binaries on a schedule and reading from AppData
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessSignatureStatus != "Valid" or ChildSHA256 !in~ (toscalar(DeviceFileCertificateInfo | where IsSigned == true and SignatureType == "CodeSign" | summarize make_set(SHA256)))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the FireAnt Metakit installer SHA256 and version from InitiatingProcessSHA256 / VersionInfoProductVersion and compare against the vendor's published known-good hash; check the timestamp against ESET's Oct-2025 to Mar-2026 supply-chain window — any install in that range is suspect by default. 2) CONTAIN: if the parent SHA256 is unknown or in the known-bad set, isolate the host, kill the process tree, and quarantine all files written by the child process in the prior 24h; alert the user to discontinue use of FireAnt Metakit pending vendor confirmation. 3) HUNT: query DeviceNetworkEvents on the host for any of the six SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains in the 7 days after the install; pivot DeviceFileEvents for files written by InitiatingProcessFolderPath of FireAnt to identify dropped stagers; check for any other endpoints in the org running FireAnt and audit their install times.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "fireant" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "fireant"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where ParentProcessName has "fireant" or ActingProcessName has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit Supply-Chain Update Spawning Suspicious Child
id: 9f1c5e22-3a7d-4f44-8e91-2f4a8b9c0d11
description: Detects the FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-investment platform spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or binaries from temp/AppData. ESET attributes a compromised-update-server supply-chain attack (Oct 2025 - Mar 2026) on this product to OceanLotus / APT32 that resulted in SPECTRALVIPER deployment.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - 'FireAnt'
      - 'Metakit'
  suspicious_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  suspicious_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
  condition: parent and (suspicious_child or suspicious_path)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@ParentImage:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit* OR *metakit*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit*)) (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\msiexec.exe) OR @Image:(*\AppData\Local\Temp\* OR *\AppData\Roaming\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *\Windows\Temp\* OR *\Users\Public\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/fireant|metakit/i OR ParentImageFileName=/(FireAnt|Metakit)/i
| (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|msiexec)\.exe$/i OR regex("\\\\(AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|AppData\\\\Roaming|ProgramData|Windows\\\\Temp|Users\\\\Public)\\\\", field=ImageFileName))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="*fireant*" OR Processes.parent_process="*FireAnt*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Metakit*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="*fireant*" OR Processes.parent_process="*FireAnt*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Metakit*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
First-seen connection to recently-registered SPECTRALVIPER-shape C2 domain AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any internal host making a first-time HTTPS connection to a domain matching the SPECTRALVIPER C&C naming pattern ESET catalogued (single-word .com domains posing as services - finance/cyber/sync/design themed), where the domain is unseen across the org's 30-day baseline. Designed to catch the next OceanLotus C2 rotation before the IOC list updates. Rationale: Uses the explicit six SPECTRALVIPER C&C domains from ESET Table 2 AND a baseline anti-join so any first-time-in-org connection to a similarly-shaped domain (finance/cyber/services themed single-word .coms — the OceanLotus naming convention) gets flagged. Catches IOC rotation that won't be in the next ESET update.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing/finance department visiting a newly-launched legitimate fintech site for the first time
  • User clicking a phishing-link analysis service that proxies through similar-shape domains
  • Threat-intel browser extension fetching from a sandbox URL
  • Internal CI/CD reaching a newly-provisioned vendor SaaS subdomain
  • Domain typosquats of legitimate companies (separate detection class)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","opera.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: enrich the matched domain with WHOIS / registration date and passive DNS - any domain registered in the last 90 days with low passive-DNS history and matching the SPECTRALVIPER naming theme is high-suspicion; check InitiatingProcessFileName to see whether it's a browser (often FP) or an unsigned binary (almost always TP). 2) CONTAIN: if non-browser process or unsigned binary, isolate the host, sinkhole the domain via DNS RPZ, and block at proxy/firewall; if browser, push the URL to your secure-browsing/SWG block-list pending vendor categorization. 3) HUNT: across the fleet, search the last 90 days for any prior connection to the same domain or any of the six known SPECTRALVIPER C&Cs; pivot on the matched host for any of the 20 SHA1 SPECTRALVIPER hashes and for FireAnt Metakit install activity.
let BaselineDomains = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
    | extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(DeviceId) by Domain
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_pattern = @"(?i)(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$";
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
| where Domain matches regex ioc_pattern or Domain matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on Domain
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, Domain, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let BaselineDomains = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(SrcIpAddr) by DnsQuery=tolower(DnsQuery)
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_known = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| extend DnsQueryLower = tolower(DnsQuery)
| where DnsQueryLower has_any (ioc_known) or DnsQueryLower matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on $left.DnsQueryLower == $right.DnsQuery
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:22 (@QueryName:(*financemachinelearning.com OR *gatewayrvcenter.com OR *coachcybersecurity.com OR *mxprodesign.com OR *power-sync-services.com OR *leadingfilipinoteams.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, FirstIP4Record], function=count(), function=min(@timestamp))
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

let BadDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
ImNetworkSession

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:

            - '\paexec.exe'

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"

        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("D511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39F", "59A8553A4F8130F576AB234E0B220BE4D4DA0E98", "9CA1A5C7F79882DB913534C1E62B26BCDCB9F6DD",        Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors. Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.

Vulnerable Baileys npm package present on disk (CVE-2026-48063 supply chain inventory) AIInstallation High
Inventories hosts that have a vulnerable Baileys distribution installed under node_modules. The advisory names two npm package identifiers — `baileys` and `@whiskeysockets/baileys` — and pins the fixed versions to 6.7.22 and 7.0.0-rc12. This hunt finds the package.json artifacts that ship with those modules so an analyst can pull the exact `version` string and compare against the vulnerable ranges. Rationale: Article explicitly names the two affected npm package identifiers (`baileys`, `@whiskeysockets/baileys`) and gives precise fixed-version anchors (6.7.22, 7.0.0-rc12). Hunting for package.json under those module paths gives the analyst the exact `version` field needed to triage. Cross-checked GHSA advisory and the linked patch commit on github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg • https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations with cloned Baileys repos used for testing
  • CI/CD build agents that materialise node_modules during pipeline runs
  • Container image scanners that mount the package tree for inspection
  • Legacy WhatsApp bot hosts running older Baileys intentionally pinned for compat
  • Personal node_modules under user profile directories (non-prod surfaces)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","node.exe") and FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\.cache\", "/tmp/"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the `version` value from the discovered package.json and confirm it falls in the vulnerable range (< 6.7.22 for v6.x, or 7.0.0-rc.1 through 7.0.0-rc11). Identify the parent Node.js application and whether it processes inbound WhatsApp messages from untrusted contacts. 2) Contain: for production WhatsApp bot/automation hosts, upgrade Baileys to 6.7.22 / 7.0.0-rc12, restart the Node process, and apply the workaround (drop messages.upsert events with a `requestId` field and set `shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false`) until the upgrade lands. 3) Hunt: pivot to other UCs in this set — search application logs for `placeholderResendMessage` and `requestId` on `messages.upsert`, and review the same host's outbound network for unusual WhatsApp WebSocket activity (g.whatsapp.net) during the suspected exposure window.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "package.json"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\baileys\", @"\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\", "/node_modules/baileys/", "/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), arg_max(Timestamp, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256) by DeviceName
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, DeviceName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "package.json"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\node_modules\baileys\", @"\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\", "/node_modules/baileys/", "/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), arg_max(TimeGenerated, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256) by DvcHostname
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Vulnerable Baileys npm Package Detected on Disk
id: 7b2a3f4c-1d5e-4a8b-9c0d-2e3f4a5b6c7d
description: Detects creation or modification of package.json under node_modules/baileys or node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys, used to inventory hosts running vulnerable Baileys versions (< 6.7.22 or < 7.0.0-rc12) affected by CVE-2026-48063 (message spoofing / app state corruption).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\node_modules\baileys\'
      - '\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\'
      - '/node_modules/baileys/'
      - '/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/'
  selection_file:
    TargetFilename|endswith: 'package.json'
  condition: selection_path and selection_file
level: low

(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@TargetFilename:(*\\node_modules\\baileys\\package.json OR *\\node_modules\\@whiskeysockets\\baileys\\package.json OR */node_modules/baileys/package.json OR */node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/package.json) OR @file.path:(*/node_modules/baileys/package.json OR */node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/package.json))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\\|\/)node_modules(\\|\/)(baileys|@whiskeysockets(\\|\/)baileys)(\\|\/)package\.json$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\baileys\\package.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\@whiskeysockets\\baileys\\package.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/baileys/package.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/package.json") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\baileys\\package.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\@whiskeysockets\\baileys\\package.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/baileys/package.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/package.json") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Baileys messages.upsert event carrying requestId field (placeholderResendMessage exploit signal) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts application logs from Node.js processes hosting Baileys for `messages.upsert` events that carry a `requestId` field — the workaround documented in the GHSA explicitly tells operators to drop these because they are the marker of a `placeholderResendMessage`-driven spoofing payload. Single-event signal with high specificity to the CVE. Rationale: The GHSA documents the workaround as 'dropping `messages.upsert` events that contain a `requestId` field' — so the presence of that field on a messages.upsert payload is, by the advisory's own framing, the actionable on-the-wire signal of the spoofing attempt. The `placeholderResendMessage` string is the named exploit vector. Both strings come directly from the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.005
Data sourcesWeb Application
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate `placeholderResendMessage` traffic — WhatsApp does use this flow in benign offline-delivery scenarios; the requestId field can appear in normal Baileys debug logging
  • Verbose Baileys debug logging shipping JSON payloads that include the literal string `messages.upsert` in unrelated log lines
  • Baileys integration test suites running in CI that exercise the placeholder-resend flow
  • Application logs at debug level dumping every websocket frame to stdout
  • Multi-tenant Baileys hosting where one tenant's normal traffic shape looks like another's anomaly
Suppression filter
| where not (SyslogMessage has "test" or SyslogMessage has "placeholder" and SyslogMessage has "debug")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full Baileys log context around the hit and the `version` reported by the host application — if version is < 6.7.22 or 7.0.0-rc.1..rc11, the message is high-confidence spoofed. Identify the remoteJid and check whether it is in the contact list of the bot/user. 2) Contain: instruct app owner to deploy the documented workaround (filter `messages.upsert` events with a `requestId` field at the handler layer) and schedule the package upgrade. If the bot took any action on the spoofed message (e.g., a workflow trigger, money movement, sensitive reply), roll those actions back. 3) Hunt: search all Baileys-hosting endpoints over the past 30 days for the same SyslogMessage signature; correlate any matches with the file-inventory UC to scope vulnerable assets.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe" or FileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("baileys", "@whiskeysockets/baileys")
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("ProcessCreated","ScriptContent","PowerShellCommand") or AdditionalFields has "messages.upsert"
    | where AdditionalFields has "messages.upsert" and (AdditionalFields has "requestId" or AdditionalFields has "placeholderResendMessage")
) on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "messages.upsert"
| where SyslogMessage has "requestId" or SyslogMessage has "placeholderResendMessage"
| extend RequestId = extract(@"requestId\"?\s*[:=]\s*\"?([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend RemoteJid = extract(@"remoteJid\"?\s*[:=]\s*\"?([0-9A-Za-z@._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, ProcessID, RequestId, RemoteJid, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:linux.syslog OR source:windows.sysmon OR @service:baileys*) @message:(*"messages.upsert"* AND (*requestId* OR *placeholderResendMessage*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/node\.exe$/i CommandLine=/baileys|@whiskeysockets\/baileys/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ScriptControlScanInfo ScriptContent=/messages\.upsert.*requestId|placeholderResendMessage/i}, field=aid, include=[ScriptContent, HostName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
# log group: /aws/lambda/<baileys-app-function>
fields @timestamp, @message, @logStream
| filter @message like /messages\.upsert/
| filter @message like /(requestId|placeholderResendMessage)/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 500
APPLICATION
`baileys_app_logs` ("messages.upsert" AND "requestId") OR ("placeholderResendMessage" AND "messages.upsert") | rex field=_raw "requestId\"?\s*[:=]\s*\"?(?<request_id>[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)" | rex field=_raw "remoteJid\"?\s*[:=]\s*\"?(?<remote_jid>[0-9A-Za-z@._-]+)" | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(remote_jid) as remote_jid values(host) as host by request_id | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | where count > 0
Suspicious history sync request shape from Baileys peer (on-demand sync spoofing) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for Baileys application logs that record on-demand or history sync events arriving from peers the host has not previously synced with, or that arrive without the corresponding outbound sync request. The GHSA explicitly calls out 'history sync spoofing which also serves the same problem, injecting fake previous context' as part of the same CVE; the operator workaround is to set `shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false`. Rationale: Article body names history sync spoofing as a distinct exploit vector of the same CVE ('injecting fake previous context or "on-demand" sync') and prescribes `shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false` as the workaround. The strings `historySync`, `messages-sync`, `history-notification`, and the workaround config flag are all Baileys-internal identifiers tied directly to this CVE's vector. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg
ATT&CKT1565.001 T1190
Data sourcesApplication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate first-time onboarding of a new device pulling its real history sync
  • Baileys integration tests exercising the historySync code paths in CI
  • Verbose debug logging that prints the workaround config flag on every startup
  • Multi-device WhatsApp account legitimately performing on-demand sync after reconnect
  • Log shippers re-replaying old log files into the SIEM (apparent duplicate sync events)
Response runbook
1) Triage: tie the history-sync log line back to a specific Baileys process and check that process's loaded `baileys` version. If vulnerable, inspect the peerJid — is it a contact the user/bot has ever conversed with? If no, treat as spoofed history injection. 2) Contain: push the workaround config (`shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false`) to that app and restart the Node process; flag the peerJid for follow-up. Plan the package upgrade in parallel. 3) Hunt: across all Baileys hosts, look for the same peerJid sending historySync to additional sessions; review the app's state store for new chat threads that materialised around the same Timestamp without a user-initiated trigger.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe" or FileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("baileys", "@whiskeysockets/baileys")
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where AdditionalFields has_any ("historySync", "history-notification", "on-demand sync", "messages-sync", "shouldSyncHistoryMessage")
) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("historySync", "history-notification", "on-demand sync", "messages-sync", "shouldSyncHistoryMessage")
| extend PeerJid = extract(@"(?:peerJid|participant|remoteJid)\"?\s*[:=]\s*\"?([0-9A-Za-z@._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend SyncType = case(
    SyslogMessage has "on-demand", "on-demand",
    SyslogMessage has "history-notification", "history-notification",
    SyslogMessage has "messages-sync", "messages-sync",
    "other")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(), Sample = any(SyslogMessage) by Computer, PeerJid, SyncType
| where Hits > 0
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:linux.syslog OR source:windows.sysmon OR @service:baileys*) @message:(*historySync* OR *"history-notification"* OR *"on-demand sync"* OR *"messages-sync"* OR *shouldSyncHistoryMessage*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/node\.exe$/i CommandLine=/baileys|@whiskeysockets\/baileys/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ScriptControlScanInfo ScriptContent=/historySync|history-notification|on-demand\s+sync|messages-sync|shouldSyncHistoryMessage/i}, field=aid, include=[ScriptContent])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/lambda/<baileys-app-function>
fields @timestamp, @message, @logStream
| filter @message like /(historySync|history-notification|on-demand sync|messages-sync|shouldSyncHistoryMessage)/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 500
APPLICATION
`baileys_app_logs` ("history-notification" OR "historySync" OR "on-demand sync" OR "shouldSyncHistoryMessage" OR "messages-sync") | rex field=_raw "(?:peerJid|participant|remoteJid)\"?\s*[:=]\s*\"?(?<peer_jid>[0-9A-Za-z@._-]+)" | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(host) as host by peer_jid | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | where count > 0
New protocolMessage type appearing in Baileys WebSocket frames AICommand & Control Low
Hunts host telemetry from Baileys-hosting Node.js processes for outbound WhatsApp WebSocket activity coinciding with locally-logged protocolMessage frames that are not part of the legitimate set the runtime version handles. The advisory describes the exploit as 'a maliciously crafted protocolMessage payload' — so a previously-unseen protocolMessage variant against a vulnerable host is the on-the-wire fingerprint of the CVE. Rationale: Article body specifies the exploit vector as a 'maliciously crafted protocolMessage payload' arriving over the Baileys WhatsApp WebSocket. Scoping host network telemetry to Node processes that have `baileys` / `@whiskeysockets/baileys` on their command line and that talk to the canonical WhatsApp WebSocket endpoints (`g.whatsapp.net`, `mmg.whatsapp.net`, `web.whatsapp.com`) gives a per-host hunt surface for follow-up packet-capture correlation when a Baileys app crash or anomalous app-state mutation occurs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Every legitimate Baileys bot run — this hunt's match set IS normal traffic, so it is only useful as a scoping list, not a standalone alert
  • Web.WhatsApp.com browser sessions from the same host (not a Baileys process at all)
  • Node tools that proxy through WhatsApp endpoints for benign reasons (analytics, testing)
  • Container hosts where the Node process command line is hidden behind a wrapper (signal lost)
  • Hosts where DNS goes through a forwarder so DeviceNetworkEvents shows the forwarder IP, not the WhatsApp endpoint
Response runbook
1) Triage: use this hunt as a host-scoping query — match the DeviceName set against the file-inventory UC's vulnerable-version list to short-list at-risk hosts. 2) Contain: for any host that is both vulnerable AND showing recent WhatsApp WebSocket activity from Baileys, push the documented workaround (filter `messages.upsert` events with `requestId`, disable history sync) and schedule the package upgrade. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same host's app logs (UCs 2 and 3) within the matching window — if a vulnerable host shows historySync or `requestId`-bearing messages.upsert events while talking to g.whatsapp.net, escalate to confirmed exploitation attempt and treat any app-state changes in that window as untrusted.
let baileys_hosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe" or FileName =~ "node.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("baileys", "@whiskeysockets/baileys")
    | distinct DeviceId, DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in (baileys_hosts)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("g.whatsapp.net", "mmg.whatsapp.net", "web.whatsapp.com")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Connections = count(), DistinctRemotes = dcount(RemoteIP), Sample = any(RemoteUrl) by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where Connections > 0
| order by LastSeen desc
let baileys_hosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has "node"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("baileys", "@whiskeysockets/baileys")
    | distinct DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (baileys_hosts)
| where DstHostname has_any ("g.whatsapp.net", "mmg.whatsapp.net", "web.whatsapp.com") or Url has_any ("g.whatsapp.net", "mmg.whatsapp.net")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Sessions = count(), DistinctDst = dcount(DstIpAddr) by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname
| where Sessions > 0
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) @process.name:node* AND (@DestinationHostname:(g.whatsapp.net OR mmg.whatsapp.net OR web.whatsapp.com) OR @network.destination.hostname:(g.whatsapp.net OR mmg.whatsapp.net OR web.whatsapp.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest ContextImageFileName=/node\.exe$/i
| DomainName=/^(g|mmg)\.whatsapp\.net$|web\.whatsapp\.com$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/node\.exe$/i CommandLine=/baileys|@whiskeysockets\/baileys/i}, field=aid, include=[CommandLine])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, CommandLine], function=count())
NETWORK

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Execution or file write of known GlassWorm / postmark-mcp sample SHA1 hashes · [LLM] npm / node postinstall hook spawning network-capable LOLBin (supply-chain post-install execution) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Dev tooling beaconing to postmark-mcp / GlassWorm campaign infrastructure (giftshop.club, sfrclak.com) · [LLM] VS Code / Cursor / node reaching Solana blockchain RPC endpoints (GlassWorm C2 channel) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Dev tooling beaconing to postmark-mcp / GlassWorm campaign infrastructure (giftshop.club, sfrclak.com) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts host-to-C2 callouts to the published Aikido IOC pack tied to the GlassWorm / postmark-mcp supply-chain compromise referenced in the article. Article-specific because it pivots on the exact IPs (142.11.206.73, 45.32.150.251, 45.32.151.157, 70.34.242.255) and domains (giftshop.club, sfrclak.com) the campaign uses for post-install exfil and second-stage download. Rationale: Direct match on the article's IOC pack: IPs 142.11.206.73, 45.32.150.251, 45.32.151.157, 70.34.242.255 and domains giftshop.club, sfrclak.com tied to the GlassWorm / postmark-mcp supply-chain compromise. Any single hit on a corporate dev endpoint is a strong post-compromise indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/intel • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel researcher / red-team detonating GlassWorm sample in an isolated lab forwarding telemetry to prod SIEM
  • Security tooling (passive DNS scanner, attack-surface monitoring service) actively resolving the domains for enrichment
  • Stale DNS cache on a host previously compromised but already remediated, replaying the resolution on TTL refresh
  • Sinkholed IP — if a takedown party now owns the IP, the destination is benign but the alert still fires
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SenseNdr.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe") or RemoteIP in (BadIPs)
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull DeviceProcessEvents around Timestamp on DeviceName to identify InitiatingProcessFileName + parent chain — confirm whether the call originated from npm/node, Code.exe, an MCP server binary, or a browser extension host. 2. CONTAIN: Isolate the device via MDE machine isolation; rotate any cloud / npm publish / SSH credentials present in the user profile (~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/, ~/.ssh/, ~/.gitconfig); revoke active session tokens for that user in Entra/Okta. 3. HUNT: Enumerate npm packages installed in the prior 24h (DeviceFileEvents on \node_modules\, package-lock.json writes) and any VS Code / Cursor extension installs (.vscode/extensions, .cursor/extensions) — fan out the same network query across the org to find peer infections.
let BadIPs = dynamic(["142.11.206.73","45.32.150.251","45.32.151.157","70.34.242.255"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["giftshop.club","sfrclak.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (BadIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity

   | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomains)
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, IndicatorType="DNS", Indicator=DnsQuery),
  (ImNetworkSession
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, IndicatorType="Network", Indicator=coalesce(DstHostname, DstIpAddr))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VS Code / Cursor / node reaching Solana blockchain RPC endpoints (GlassWorm C2 channel) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts developer-tooling processes (Code.exe, Cursor.exe, node.exe, npm.exe) resolving or connecting to public Solana RPC infrastructure within a 5-minute window. The GlassWorm supply-chain attack referenced in the article uses Solana on-chain transactions as a resilient dead-drop C2 channel — a dev IDE talking to Solana RPC is rarely legitimate outside crypto-product teams. Rationale: GlassWorm (referenced by name in the article) is publicly documented to use Solana on-chain reads as a dead-drop C2 fetch — pinning the detection to dev IDEs and node runtime restricts the otherwise-noisy Solana DNS signal to the exact attack shape: a compromised VS Code/Cursor extension or npm postinstall script fetching its next-stage URL from a Solana transaction memo. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/ • https://blog.koi.security/ • https://www.aikido.dev/intel
ATT&CKT1102 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineers working on crypto / Web3 product lines whose dev workflows legitimately call Solana RPC
  • Developers running local @solana/web3.js test suites or hardhat/anchor toolchain
  • VS Code extensions for Solana development (e.g. Solana Developer Tools) doing legitimate RPC calls
  • node-based browser preview / linter background process bundling a wallet SDK fixture
Suppression filter
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("@solana/web3.js","@coral-xyz/anchor","--web3-test","hardhat")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Identify the parent of the dev-tool process — if it's electron/Code.exe spawned by a child extension host with --extension-id, capture the extension ID from CommandLine and check the marketplace for recent updates / takedowns. Inspect ~/.vscode/extensions and ~/.cursor/extensions for newly installed or recently updated packages. 2. CONTAIN: Isolate the device. Revoke npm publish tokens, GitHub PATs, and cloud creds in the user profile. Disable the suspect extension org-wide if a malicious extension ID is confirmed. 3. HUNT: Pivot on the extension ID across the fleet via DeviceFileEvents for the extension's manifest path; pivot on RemoteIP returned by the Solana DNS to find direct IP callouts that skipped DNS.
let SolanaDomains = dynamic(["solana.com","mainnet-beta.solana.com","api.mainnet-beta.solana.com","api.devnet.solana.com","api.testnet.solana.com","helius.xyz","helius-rpc.com","solscan.io","solana-rpc.com","genesysgo.net","quicknode.com"]);
let DevTools = dynamic(["Code.exe","Cursor.exe","node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","WindsurfNext.exe","electron.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (DevTools)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (SolanaDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let SolanaDomains = dynamic(["solana.com","mainnet-beta.solana.com","api.mainnet-beta.solana.com","api.devnet.solana.com","api.testnet.solana.com","helius.xyz","helius-rpc.com","solscan.io","solana-rpc.com","genesysgo.net","quicknode.com"]);
let DevTools = dynamic(["Code.exe","Cursor.exe","node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","WindsurfNext.exe","electron.exe"]);
let WindowMin = 5m;
let DnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (SolanaDomains)
    | project DnsTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any (DevTools)
| extend HostKey = coalesce(DvcHostname, "")
| join kind=inner (DnsHits | extend HostKey = coalesce(DvcHostname, SrcHostname, "")) on HostKey
| where TimeGenerated between (DnsTime - WindowMin .. DnsTime + WindowMin)
| project TimeGenerated, DnsTime, HostKey, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, DnsQuery
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Execution or file write of known GlassWorm / postmark-mcp sample SHA1 hashes AIInstallation High
Direct hash IOC match on the three SHA1s shipped with the article: 2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca, d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71, 07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766. Covers both execution (process create) and on-disk landing (file write) so we catch drops that haven't run yet. Rationale: The article ships three SHA1 hashes tied to the campaign discussed (GlassWorm / postmark-mcp). Direct hash hits on workstation telemetry are the highest-confidence signal we can ship — any positive is investigation-worthy regardless of process context. Cross-checked against: • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/ • https://bazaar.abuse.ch/ • https://www.aikido.dev/intel
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR / malware analyst detonating one of these samples in a sandbox VM that ships telemetry to the production tenant
  • Threat-intel feed downloading samples to a designated analyst workstation for triage
  • Defender / Falcon sample-submission service caching the file in a quarantine path that still emits a FileWritten event
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Confirm the host is a real developer workstation (not a malware-analysis VM). Pull DeviceProcessEvents within ±5 min of the hash hit to identify what wrote it (npm install? a VS Code extension install? a Slack file download?) and what subsequently spawned. 2. CONTAIN: Immediately isolate via MDE/Falcon; rotate ALL credentials present in the user profile — npm publish tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS access keys, SSH keys, GPG signing keys, cloud SSO refresh tokens. Force re-auth across SSO. 3. HUNT: Pivot on the source package name (if npm postinstall — check ~/.npm/_logs and the parent npm command) and search the org for the same package install. Check git push activity from this workstation in the last 7 days for unreviewed pushes — assume any commits/publishes since first hash sighting are tainted.
let BadSHA1 = dynamic(["2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca","d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71","07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
   | where SHA1 in (BadSHA1) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (BadSHA1)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA1, ProcessCommandLine, IndicatorType="ProcessExec"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
   | where SHA1 in (BadSHA1)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, IndicatorType="FileWrite")
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadSHA1 = dynamic(["2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca","d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71","07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
   | where SHA1 in (BadSHA1) or Hash in (BadSHA1)
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, SHA1, IndicatorType="ProcessExec"),
  (ImFileEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
   | where TargetFileSHA1 in (BadSHA1) or Hash in (BadSHA1)
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1, IndicatorType="FileWrite")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm / node postinstall hook spawning network-capable LOLBin (supply-chain post-install execution) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the exact attack shape the article calls out: 'agent merges the PR, pulls a new dependency, executes the postinstall hook, and touches production credentials.' Fires when node.exe / npm.exe is the parent of an interpreter or download utility executing a network-fetch command within seconds of an install. Covers the silent malicious-MCP-server-on-npm scenario referenced in the article (15 clean versions, backdoor on the 16th). Rationale: Article explicitly describes this attack chain ('the agent merges the PR, pulls a new dependency, executes the postinstall hook, and touches production credentials') and references the September 2025 malicious-MCP-server-on-npm campaign. The parent (node/npm) + child (interpreter/download LOLBin) + cmdline-fetch-token triple is the precise behavioural shape of a malicious package postinstall. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/016/ • https://sigmahq.io/ • https://socket.dev/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate node-based build tools (electron-builder, node-gyp, prebuild-install) that download platform binaries during install
  • Husky / lint-staged git hooks invoking PowerShell to format files
  • CI agents on dev workstations running 'npm install' that fetch architecture-specific binaries via curl in their postinstall
  • Native module compilation flows (node-gyp → MSBuild) that shell out to download SDK headers
  • Cypress / Playwright postinstall downloading browser bundles via curl
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("node-gyp","electron-builder","prebuild-install","cypress install","playwright install","husky","lint-staged") and ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("electron-v","prebuilds/","cypress.zip","playwright-core")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the full parent chain — InitiatingProcessParentFileName and one level up — to identify the npm invocation context. Extract the registry URL / package name from ~/.npm/_logs/*-debug.log around Timestamp and check the package on socket.dev or deps.dev for malicious indicators (recent maintainer change, sudden version bump from clean to backdoored). 2. CONTAIN: Isolate the device. Treat every credential on the workstation as compromised — rotate npm publish tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS/GCP creds, SSH keys, cloud SSO sessions. If the package was published by an org-pinned maintainer, escalate to the registry security team for takedown. 3. HUNT: Org-wide search for the same package name + version across DeviceFileEvents on node_modules paths; for any other host that installed the same version, repeat steps 1–2. Pivot on the destination URL from the child cmdline to the GlassWorm / postmark-mcp IOC hunt (UC 1).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","Invoke-RestMethod","IEX","iwr","http://","https://","curl ","wget ","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","urlcache","bitsadmin /transfer","BITSADMIN")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentName = tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| extend ChildName = tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where tolower(ParentName) in ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where tolower(ChildName) in ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","Invoke-RestMethod","IEX","iwr","http://","https://","curl ","wget ","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","urlcache","bitsadmin /transfer")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, ParentName, NewProcessName, ChildName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm/node Postinstall Hook Spawns Network-Capable LOLBin
id: a3d77f01-9e58-4f7b-b612-glassworm0003
description: Detects node/npm spawning a Windows interpreter or download utility with network-fetch commandline tokens — typical of malicious postinstall hooks in compromised npm / MCP packages.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/code-is-written-everywhere
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1546.016
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
  cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'Invoke-RestMethod'
      - 'IEX'
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - 'urlcache'
      - 'bitsadmin /transfer'
  condition: parent and child and cmd
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\npx.exe) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\mshta.exe) @CommandLine:(*DownloadString* OR *Invoke-WebRequest* OR *Invoke-RestMethod* OR *http://* OR *https://* OR *-EncodedCommand* OR *urlcache* OR *bitsadmin*transfer*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|curl|wget|certutil|bitsadmin|mshta)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(DownloadString|Invoke-WebRequest|Invoke-RestMethod|IEX|iwr|http://|https://|curl |wget |-EncodedCommand|urlcache|bitsadmin /transfer)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable go-base deployment: AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random in process command-line AIInstallation High
Hunts for processes launched with the hardcoded weak JWT signing key from CVE-2026-48031 (dhax/go-base). Any service started with AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random is trivially exploitable — an attacker reading the public repo can forge admin JWTs in seconds. Surfaces the vulnerable deployment before exploitation occurs. Rationale: Pivots on the exact literal string from dev.env:10 and cmd/serve.go:35 — the article explicitly states this is the hardcoded default that ships to all users. Process command-lines capture both the env-var prefix form (AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random env -- ./serve) and Viper-resolved dump output. Corroborated via the linked fix PR #31 which removes exactly this string. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running the unpatched boilerplate on a workstation while learning the framework
  • CI/CD job for the go-base reference app intentionally exercising the vulnerable path
  • Security researcher reproducing CVE-2026-48031 in an isolated lab
  • Internal CTF / training environment using the boilerplate as a teaching artifact
  • Stale containers from before the May 2026 patch still running in non-prod
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Users\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains @"\dev\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains @"\sandbox\" and DeviceName !has "-dev" and DeviceName !has "-lab"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm the host's role — is this a production API, staging, or a dev box? Pull the parent process chain to identify the orchestrator (systemd, kubelet, docker-compose). Check whether the binary path resolves to a go-base derivative (`go-base`, `serve`, project name in folder path). 2) CONTAIN: if production or internet-facing, stop the service immediately; rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to `openssl rand -base64 32`; invalidate all existing tokens server-side. If still dev, file a vuln ticket and gate deployment. 3) HUNT: scan all hosts for the same string; pivot to web access logs for the affected service and run UC2/UC3 against the same window to determine whether forgery attempts already landed; check git history for any internal forks of dhax/go-base still pinned below the PR#31 commit.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where EventID == 4688
   | where CommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
             Process = NewProcessName, CommandLine,
             ParentProcess = ParentProcessName),
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
        or ParentProcessCommandLine has "AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random"
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername,
             Process = ActingProcessName, CommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine,
             ParentProcess = ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
